木不能至拱把無源之水不能達江河非
務本之論也弗去其耗則山林不能供野
火江海不能實漏卮非救時之策也故必
力本而導利有以開財之源酌盈以濟虛
有以節財之流則不必規規於理財而財
自充國自富矣請因明問而復之易曰何
以守位曰仁何以聚人曰財言足國裕民
惟財爲急也書曰水火金木土穀惟修正
德利用厚生惟和言阜財養民惟政爲先
punctuated:
同考試官進士李批：理財一事，方今急務。子能詳悉古今失得，而惓惓於節用，是有經國之慮者，宜錄以式。

考試官右贊善閻批：叅論古今理財得失，若指諸掌。中間區畫數事，皆鑿鑿可行，有學有用之士也。

考試官侍講康批：理財，人能言之。是作考論古今盈縮之故，而裁以獨見，且通達國體，諳練時務，豈韋布而有天下之慮者耶？

愚聞之：天下之財，其豐也，固必有其源；而其耗也，亦必有其由。弗開其源，則無根之木不能至拱把，無源之水不能達江河，非務本之論也。弗去其耗，則山林不能供野火，江海不能實漏卮，非救時之策也。故必力本而導利，有以開財之源；酌盈以濟虛，有以節財之流。則不必規規於理財，而財自充，國自富矣。請因明問而復之。《易》曰：「何以守位？曰仁。何以聚人？曰財。」言足國裕民，惟財爲急也。《書》曰：「水火金木土穀惟修，正德利用厚生惟和。」言阜財養民，惟政爲先
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Li, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), comments: Managing finances is an urgent task today. You understand thoroughly the successes and failures of past and present and are deeply concerned with economy in expenditure. You thus show concern for governing the state; this essay should be recorded as a model.

Examiner Yan, Right Admonisher, comments: The comparative discussion of successes and failures in financial administration, past and present, makes them as clear as something pointed out in one's palm. The several measures proposed in the middle of the essay are all demonstrably practicable. Here is a man of learning and practical ability.

Examiner Kang, Expositor, comments: Anyone can speak of managing finances. This essay examines the causes of abundance and shortage in past and present and judges them with independent insight. Moreover, it shows a thorough understanding of the principles of state governance and familiarity with current affairs. Could this be a man in commoner's clothing who nevertheless concerns himself with all under Heaven?

I have heard that the wealth of all under Heaven, when abundant, must certainly have its source; and when depleted, must likewise have its cause. Unless its source is opened up, a rootless tree cannot grow to a girth that one's hands can encircle, and water without a source cannot reach the great rivers. Such an approach fails to attend to fundamentals. Unless the causes of depletion are removed, mountain forests cannot keep a wildfire supplied, nor can rivers and seas fill a leaking goblet. Such an approach offers no remedy for the needs of the age. One must therefore devote effort to fundamental production and foster its benefits, thereby opening up the sources of wealth; one must draw upon surpluses to make good deficiencies, thereby regulating the outflow of wealth. Then, without having to attend narrowly to financial management, resources will naturally become plentiful and the state wealthy. Allow me to respond to your discerning question on this basis. The Book of Changes says: “How is one's position maintained? Through benevolence. How are people gathered together? Through wealth.” This means that, in supplying the state adequately and enriching the people, wealth is the urgent concern. The Book of Documents says: “Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain must be duly managed; rectifying virtue, facilitating use, and enriching livelihoods must be harmonized.” This means that, in increasing wealth and sustaining the people, governance takes priority…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也考之成周理財之法備載周禮既有太
宰司徒以制出入矣又有司會司書職內
職歲職幣之官既有六典八法八則以達
治矣又立九貢九賦九式九職之法樞機
之周密也如此以叅互攷日成以月要攷
月成以歲會攷歲成制用之有節也如此
有理財之實而無其名故當其時富蔵億
兆之室禄養千八百國之君君有餘財民
有餘力而頌聲作經世足國之法莫有善
===
於此者自周官之法廢而聚斂之臣始擅
理財之名自理財之說興而天下之民始
受兼并之禍於漢吾得一人焉曰桑弘羊
方武帝時東征西伐海內虛耗乃作平準
之法受天下之轉輸籠天下之財物貴則
賣之賤則買之欲使富商大賈無所牟大
利而萬物不得騰踊卒之筭舟車告緡錢
榷鹽酒無補於民力之告竭而漢祚蹙矣
於唐吾得一人焉曰劉晏當德宗時兩河

治矣又立九貢九賦九式九職之法樞機
之周密也如此以參互攷日成以月要攷
月成以歲會攷歲成制用之有節也如此
有理財之實而無其名故當其時富藏億
兆之室祿養千八百國之君君有餘財民
有餘力而頌聲作經世足國之法莫有善
===
於此者自周官之法廢而聚歛之臣始擅
理財之名自理財之說興而天下之民始
受兼并之禍於漢吾得一人焉曰桑弘羊
方武帝時東征西伐海內虛耗乃作平準
之法受天下之轉輸籠天下之財物貴則
賣之賤則買之欲使富商大賈無所牟大
利而萬物不得騰踊卒之筭舟車告緡錢
榷鹽酒無補於民力之告竭而漢祚㦯矣
於唐吾得一人焉曰劉晏當德宗時兩河
punctuated:
也。考之成周，理財之法備載《周禮》。既有太宰、司徒以制出入矣，又有司會、司書、職內、職歲、職幣之官。既有六典、八法、八則以達治矣，又立九貢、九賦、九式、九職之法。樞機之周密也如此。以叅互攷日成，以月要攷月成，以歲會攷歲成，制用之有節也如此。有理財之實而無其名，故當其時，富蔵億兆之室，禄養千八百國之君，君有餘財，民有餘力，而頌聲作。經世足國之法，莫有善於此者。
自周官之法廢，而聚斂之臣始擅理財之名；自理財之說興，而天下之民始受兼并之禍。於漢，吾得一人焉，曰桑弘羊。方武帝時，東征西伐，海內虛耗，乃作平準之法，受天下之轉輸，籠天下之財物，貴則賣之，賤則買之，欲使富商大賈無所牟大利，而萬物不得騰踊。卒之筭舟車、告緡錢、榷鹽酒，無補於民力之告竭，而漢祚蹙矣。
於唐，吾得一人焉，曰劉晏。當德宗時，兩河
translation_en:
… indeed. Examining the institutions of the Zhou, we find their methods of managing wealth fully recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). They had the Grand Steward and the Minister of Education to regulate receipts and expenditures, as well as officials serving as Controller of Accounts, Keeper of Records, Director of Receipts, Director of Annual Accounts, and Director of Surplus Funds. They had six canons, eight administrative rules, and eight regulations to carry government into effect, and also established systems of nine categories of tribute, nine categories of taxation, nine standards of expenditure, and nine occupations. Such was the thoroughness of their administrative machinery. They examined daily accomplishments through cross-checking, monthly accomplishments through monthly summaries, and annual accomplishments through annual accounts. Such was their discipline in regulating expenditure. They practiced the substance of managing wealth without claiming the name. Thus, in those days, wealth was stored in the households of the countless people, and revenues supported the rulers of eighteen hundred states. Rulers had wealth to spare, the people had strength to spare, and songs of praise arose. No method of ordering the world and providing adequately for the state surpassed this.
Once the institutions of the Zhou officials were abandoned, ministers bent on exaction began to arrogate to themselves the name of financial management. Once doctrines of financial management arose, the people of the realm began to suffer the calamities of wealth being engrossed by the powerful. In the Han, I find one such man: Sang Hongyang. During Emperor Wu’s reign, campaigns east and west depleted the realm. Sang therefore instituted the price-stabilization system, receiving goods transported from throughout the realm and bringing its wealth and commodities under his control. He sold when prices were high and bought when they were low, intending to prevent wealthy merchants and great traders from making excessive profits and to keep commodity prices from soaring. In the end, taxes on boats and carts, denunciations of unreported taxable wealth, and monopolies on salt and alcoholic drink did nothing to remedy the exhaustion of the people’s resources, and the fortunes of the Han dynasty contracted.
In the Tang, I find one such man: Liu Yan. During Emperor Dezong’s reign, the two He regions…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
用兵經費告匱乃用平準之法斡山海排
商賈制萬物低昂操天下贏貲以佐軍興
變通有無曲盡其妙然專利召禍身歿之
後鹽鐵轉運和糴括商錢稅間架規利無
餘府庫不支數月而唐祚衰矣於宋吾得
一人焉曰吕惠卿方神宗時用兵河朔國
用不足乃行泉府之法以收利權以常平
糴本散之小民令出息二分春散秋斂謂
之青苗然出納之際吏緣為姦均輸之政
===
自同商賈手實之禍下及雞豚他如行助
役求水利興事起新囂然不寧肇成靖康
之禍而宋業隳矣夫三代以上理財莫善
於周故民足而國亦足三代以下理財莫
不善於漢唐宋故民窮而國亦窮所以然
者蓋財猶泉也泉行而不可壅利布而不
可專以天下之財與天下共理之則民富
而君不能獨貧取天下之利而專之於上
則民貧而君不能獨富此固成周之所以

役求水利興事起新嚻然不寧肇成靖康
之禍而宋業隳矣夫三代以上理財莫善

而君不能獨貧取天下之利而專之於上
則民貧而君不能獨富此固成周之所以
punctuated:
用兵，經費告匱，乃用平準之法，斡山海，排商賈，制萬物低昂，操天下贏貲，以佐軍興。變通有無，曲盡其妙，然專利召禍。身歿之後，鹽鐵、轉運、和糴、括商錢、稅間架，規利無餘，府庫不支數月，而唐祚衰矣。於宋吾得一人焉，曰吕惠卿。方神宗時，用兵河朔，國用不足，乃行泉府之法，以收利權。以常平糴本散之小民，令出息二分，春散秋斂，謂之青苗。然出納之際，吏緣為姦；均輸之政，自同商賈；手實之禍，下及雞豚。他如行助役，求水利，興事起新，囂然不寧，肇成靖康之禍，而宋業隳矣。
夫三代以上，理財莫善於周，故民足而國亦足；三代以下，理財莫不善於漢唐宋，故民窮而國亦窮。所以然者，蓋財猶泉也，泉行而不可壅，利布而不可專。以天下之財，與天下共理之，則民富而君不能獨貧；取天下之利，而專之於上，則民貧而君不能獨富。此固成周之所以
translation_en:
…troops were engaged in war, and funds for expenditures ran short. He therefore employed the price-stabilization system, exploiting the resources of mountains and seas, squeezing out merchants, controlling the rise and fall of commodity prices, and commanding the realm’s surplus wealth to support military operations. In adjusting supplies to meet shortages, he displayed every subtlety of the art; yet monopolizing profits brought disaster. After his death, salt and iron monopolies, transport administration, government grain purchases, the exaction of merchants’ cash, and taxes on rooms and buildings exhausted every means of extracting revenue. Still, the treasury could not cover even several months’ expenses, and the Tang dynasty declined. In the Song, I find one such man: Lü Huiqing. During Shenzong’s reign, troops were campaigning in Heshuo, and state revenues were insufficient. He therefore implemented the system of the Treasury of Exchange (quanfu) to bring control over profits into government hands. He distributed among the common people the funds earmarked for grain purchases by the ever-normal granaries, requiring interest of twenty percent. Loans were issued in spring and collected in autumn; this was called the Green Sprouts system. Yet officials exploited the issuing and collecting of loans to commit fraud; through the equitable transport policy, the government itself acted like a merchant; and the harm caused by declarations of household property extended even to chickens and pigs. Other measures, such as implementing service-assistance payments and pursuing irrigation projects, launched new undertakings and innovations, producing uproar and unrest. These laid the foundations for the Jingkang catastrophe, and the Song’s imperial achievement was brought to ruin.
Through the age of the Three Dynasties, none managed finances better than the Zhou; thus the people had enough, and the state likewise had enough. After the Three Dynasties, none managed finances worse than the Han, Tang, and Song; thus the people were impoverished, and the state likewise was impoverished. The reason is that wealth resembles a spring: its waters must flow and cannot be dammed up; benefits must circulate and cannot be monopolized. If the wealth of the realm is managed together with all the people of the realm, the people will prosper, and the ruler cannot alone remain poor. If the profits of the realm are taken and monopolized by those above, the people will be poor, and the ruler cannot alone remain rich. This, indeed, is why the Zhou…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
興而漢唐宋之所以不競也然觀句踐之
治越也用計然之策財貨充溢國以富強
卒能觀兵伐吳取威定霸范蠡謂計然之
策七越用其五而得意既以施之國吾欲
施之家今考其術不過知闘則脩備時用
則知物旱則資舟水則資車貴出如糞土
賤取如珠玉擇人任時農末俱利審積著
之理觀萬貨之情此其大較也即使盡用
之亦不過桑劉惠卿之故智欲以富國而
===
非以富民也彼其卧薪甞膽卒成富強豈
盡繫於計然之策哉吾聞征利之說不聞
於豐大之國孅孅然與民爭利者匹夫之
事非所施於天下之術也君子又何取焉
仰惟我
國家立法定制則壤成賦有郡國以歲上其
計有司徒以專掌其權取之有時用之有
節藹然成周之遺意也而幅員之廣從古
所無東南財賦歲輸四百萬昔人謂之陸

盡繫於計然之策哉吾聞征利之說不聞
於豐大之國嬓嬓然與民爭利者匹夫之
事非所施於天下之術也君子又何取焉
仰惟我
國家立法定制則壤成賦有郡國以歲上其
計有司徒以專掌其權取之有時用之有
節藹然成周之遺意也而幅員之廣從古
所無東南財賦歲輸四百萬昔人謂之陸
punctuated:
興，而漢唐宋之所以不競也。然觀句踐之治越也，用計然之策，財貨充溢，國以富強，卒能觀兵伐吳，取威定霸。范蠡謂：「計然之策七，越用其五而得意。既以施之國，吾欲施之家。」今考其術，不過知闘則脩備，時用則知物，旱則資舟，水則資車，貴出如糞土，賤取如珠玉，擇人任時，農末俱利，審積著之理，觀萬貨之情，此其大較也。即使盡用之，亦不過桑劉惠卿之故智，欲以富國而非以富民也。彼其卧薪甞膽，卒成富強，豈盡繫於計然之策哉？吾聞征利之說不聞於豐大之國，孅孅然與民爭利者，匹夫之事，非所施於天下之術也。君子又何取焉？
仰惟我國家立法定制，則壤成賦，有郡國以歲上其計，有司徒以專掌其權，取之有時，用之有節，藹然成周之遺意也。而幅員之廣，從古所無，東南財賦歲輸四百萬，昔人謂之陸
translation_en:
…flourished, whereas the Han, Tang, and Song failed to remain strong. Yet consider Goujian’s government of Yue: by employing Ji Ran’s policies, he filled it with wealth and goods and made the state rich and powerful. In the end he could muster his forces and attack Wu, establish his prestige, and secure hegemony. Fan Li said: “Ji Ran had seven policies. Yue employed five of them and achieved its aims. Having applied them to the state, I now wish to apply them to my household.” Examining these methods now, we find that they amounted only to making preparations when conflict was foreseen; understanding goods in relation to their seasonal uses; acquiring boats in drought and carts in flood; selling goods when dear as though they were dung, and buying them when cheap as though they were pearls and jade; choosing suitable people and taking advantage of the right moment; securing profits from both agriculture and commerce; examining the principles of accumulating stocks; and observing the conditions governing all commodities. Such was their general outline. Even if all these methods were employed, they would amount to no more than the old devices of Sang, Liu, and Huiqing, intended to enrich the state rather than the people. Goujian slept on brushwood and tasted gall, and eventually attained wealth and power: could this have depended entirely on Ji Ran’s policies? I have heard that doctrines of seeking profit find no hearing in an abundant and great state. Pettily competing with the people for profit is the business of a private individual, not a method to be applied to governing all under Heaven. What, then, would a gentleman find worthy of adoption in it?
I respectfully consider how our dynasty has established laws and fixed institutions, assessing tribute according to the soil. Its regional administrations submit their accounts annually, while the Minister of Revenue exercises exclusive authority over these matters. Revenue is collected at the proper times and expenditure kept within limits: the spirit inherited from the Zhou is abundantly evident. Moreover, the extent of our territory is unparalleled since antiquity. The southeast annually remits four million in tax revenues. People of old called it a “land…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
海宜無空乏之慮矣矧我
聖天子軫念元元優恤蠲貸深仁濊澤有三代
之風而司計之臣歛散出入成法具存又
無漢唐宋言利之臣之失宜其財用之日
益滋也夫何邇年以來田野之間家無蓋
蔵太倉之積不支數歲兼之光祿之厨料
太僕之馬價動稱缺乏雖徵積歲之逋開
上納之例而度支經費尚爾告匱近者修
邊之需司徒本兵至相推避此豈太平之
===
世所宜有哉無亦中外奉法之臣猶有未
盡者乎兹欲圖所以足財之策無他亦惟
濬其源而去其耗而已今之為財之源者
有四而所以為財之耗者亦有四天下之
農徵輸煩擾十室九空加以水旱之不時
吏胥之科尅眼瘡未醫心肉再剜故恤農
之政不可不行也京師以東蔡鄧齊魯之
間三代財賦多出乎此漢唐以來所以開
田興利溝洫封澮之跡往往猶存而今悉

邊之需司徒本兵至相推避此豈太平之
===

盡者乎兹欲圖所以足財之策無他亦惟

有四而所以爲財之耗者亦有四天下之

之政不可不行也京師以東蔡鄧齊魯之
閒三代財賦多出乎此漢唐以来所以開
田興利溝洫封澮之跡往往猶存而今悉
punctuated:
海，宜無空乏之慮矣。矧我聖天子軫念元元，優恤蠲貸，深仁濊澤，有三代之風。而司計之臣，歛散出入，成法具存，又無漢唐宋言利之臣之失，宜其財用之日益滋也。夫何邇年以來，田野之間，家無蓋蔵，太倉之積不支數歲？兼之光祿之厨料、太僕之馬價，動稱缺乏。雖徵積歲之逋，開上納之例，而度支經費尚爾告匱。近者修邊之需，司徒、本兵至相推避，此豈太平之世所宜有哉？無亦中外奉法之臣猶有未盡者乎？
兹欲圖所以足財之策，無他，亦惟濬其源而去其耗而已。今之為財之源者有四，而所以為財之耗者亦有四。天下之農，徵輸煩擾，十室九空，加以水旱之不時、吏胥之科尅，眼瘡未醫，心肉再剜，故恤農之政不可不行也。
京師以東，蔡鄧齊魯之間，三代財賦多出乎此。漢唐以來，所以開田興利，溝洫封澮之跡，往往猶存，而今悉
translation_en:
…a “sea on land”; surely there should be no fear of want. Moreover, our sagely Son of Heaven cares deeply for the common people, generously relieving their distress through tax remissions and loans. His profound benevolence and abundant beneficence recall the Three Dynasties. The ministers responsible for fiscal affairs have established regulations governing collection and disbursement, receipts and expenditures. Nor have they committed the errors of the ministers who advocated profit-seeking under the Han, Tang, and Song. Financial resources ought therefore to grow more abundant by the day. Why, then, in recent years have rural households had no stores laid by, while the reserves of the Grand Granary cannot sustain even a few years? Moreover, shortages are constantly reported in the provisions for the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the horse-purchase funds of the Court of the Imperial Stud. Although arrears accumulated over successive years have been collected and provisions for making contributions to the state have been instituted, funds for regular government expenditure are still reported exhausted. Recently, over the funds needed to repair the frontier defenses, the Minister of Revenue and the Minister of War have even sought to shift responsibility onto one another. How can such things be fitting in an age of peace? Might the officials charged with upholding the laws, both at court and in the provinces, still be failing to discharge their duties fully?
To devise a policy that will make financial resources sufficient requires nothing else than deepening their sources and eliminating their drains. Today there are four sources of revenue and likewise four drains upon it. Throughout the realm, farmers are harassed by burdensome demands for tax payments and deliveries; nine households in ten are destitute. Added to this are unpredictable floods and droughts and the exactions of officials and clerks. Before the sore at the eye has healed, flesh is gouged once more from the heart. Policies to relieve farmers must therefore be put into effect.
East of the capital, in the regions of Cai, Deng, Qi, and Lu, much of the revenue of the Three Dynasties originated. Traces of the works used since the Han and Tang to open farmland and develop its productive benefits—ditches, channels, embankments [?], and main waterways—often still survive. Yet now all …

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
為萑葦之地使北人仰給東南一有凶荒
張口待哺故山澤之利不可不墾也古者
用民之力歲不過三日今則郡邑之吏徵
發之不時期會之無節一人耕之十人聚
而食之欲末技游食之民轉而緣南畝不
可得已故力役之征不可不節也自屯政
既廢塞下蕩然無有積貯一兵以上皆仰
給於縣官欲農民不困不可得已故屯田
之政不可不脩也此豐財之源也若夫
===
宗藩之支庶日繁而禄米之歲輸不給日復
一日後將難繼則嚴妾媵之制殺親盡之
等開衣食之原者不可以不處也府史胥
徒中外充斥丞尉佐貳郡縣增設蘇軾所
謂一官而三人共者冗員不可不汰也屯
衞之軍尺籍雖存而逃亡將半監局工匠
冗濫未革而廩食浩繁冗食不可不省也
漕河兌運公取其一私或倍之邊儲濟助
軍得其一官或倍之京師之一金田野之

用民之力歲不過三日今則郡邑之吏徵
發之不時期會之無節一人耕之十人聚
而食之欲末技游食之民轉而緣南畝不
可得已故力役之征不可不節也自屯政
既廢塞下蕩然無有積貯一兵以上皆仰
給於縣官欲農民不困不可得已故屯田
之政不可不脩也此豐財之源也若夫
===
宗藩之支庶日繁而祿米之歲輸不給日復
一日後將難繼則嚴妾媵之制殺親盡之
等開衣食之原者不可以不處也府史胥
徒中外充斥丞尉佐貳郡縣增設蘇軾所
謂一官而三人共者冗員不可不汰也屯
衛之軍尺籍雖存而逃亡將半監局工匠
冗濫未革而廩食浩繁冗食不可不省也
漕河宂運公取其一私或倍之邊儲濟助
軍得其一官或倍之京師之一金田野之
punctuated:
為萑葦之地，使北人仰給東南，一有凶荒，張口待哺。故山澤之利不可不墾也。古者用民之力，歲不過三日；今則郡邑之吏，徵發之不時，期會之無節，一人耕之，十人聚而食之，欲末技游食之民轉而緣南畝，不可得已。故力役之征不可不節也。自屯政既廢，塞下蕩然，無有積貯，一兵以上皆仰給於縣官，欲農民不困，不可得已。故屯田之政不可不脩也。此豐財之源也。
若夫宗藩之支庶日繁，而禄米之歲輸不給，日復一日，後將難繼，則嚴妾媵之制、殺親盡之等、開衣食之原者，不可以不處也。府史胥徒，中外充斥；丞尉佐貳，郡縣增設。蘇軾所謂一官而三人共者，冗員不可不汰也。屯衞之軍，尺籍雖存，而逃亡將半；監局工匠，冗濫未革，而廩食浩繁。冗食不可不省也。漕河兌運，公取其一，私或倍之；邊儲濟助，軍得其一，官或倍之。京師之一金，田野之
translation_en:
…have become reed beds, making the people of the north dependent on supplies from the southeast. Whenever famine strikes, they can only open their mouths and wait to be fed. Thus the resources of mountains and marshes must be developed. In antiquity, the people's labor was requisitioned for no more than three days a year. Now prefectural and county officials impose levies at irregular times and set deadlines without restraint. One person tills the land, while ten gather to eat its produce. Under such conditions, it is impossible to induce people engaged in subsidiary crafts or living idly at others' expense to turn to working the fields. Thus compulsory labor services must be limited. Since the abandonment of the military agricultural colony system, the frontier has been utterly depleted, with no accumulated reserves. Every soldier depends on the government for supplies; it is impossible for the farming population to escape distress. Thus the military agricultural colony system must be restored. These are the sources from which public wealth may be increased.
As for the collateral branches of the imperial clan, their numbers grow daily, while annual deliveries of stipend grain fall short. As this continues day after day, it will eventually become impossible to sustain. Measures must therefore be devised to tighten regulations governing concubines, reduce the grades of entitlement of those whose kinship ties have grown remote, and open up sources of livelihood. Clerks, scribes, subclerks, and runners crowd the central and local administrations; additional assistant magistrates, defenders, and other subordinate officials are established in prefectures and counties. This is what Su Shi called having three people share a single office. Superfluous personnel must be dismissed. Among the troops of the agricultural colonies and guards, although the muster rolls remain, nearly half have deserted. Among the artisans of the directorates and bureaus, excessive and irregular staffing has yet to be corrected, and expenditure on their provisions is enormous. Superfluous recipients of government support must be reduced. In the transfer and transport of grain along the Grand Canal, for every unit taken officially, perhaps twice as much is taken privately. In aid for frontier supplies, for every unit the soldiers receive, officials may take twice as much. One unit of money in the capital, in the countryside…

…a hundred measures of gold. A hundred measures of gold in the public treasury represent ten thousand in the households of the people. Thus, superfluous expenditure must be curtailed. This is how to eliminate the drains on wealth. As for the root of the matter, it lies in Our Emperor’s rectifying the guiding principles and rules of government from above, so that the high ministers and officials possess the integrity celebrated in “The Lamb” (Gao yang), and the common people follow the ethos of “The Cricket” (Xi shuai). title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
禁中頗牧者耶
禦邊之畧有要焉而泛者不與也有機焉
而滯者不與也有無形之險焉而周防曲
護者不與也夫事幾之動其變無常議之
者適中其肯綮之會是之謂要以天下非
常之事付之以非常之才使之畢力以圖
其成是之謂機委之專任之久俾上下之
志固結而不可解是之謂險是故務安攘
之大計而不恬於旦夕之安則其要得矣
===
羅一世之豪傑而鼓舞之假之以便宜而
不撓于中制則其機運矣人心思奮以必
勝為期使敵人畏之而不敢犯則無形之
險在我矣否則其備彌周其道彌遠其慮
彌悉其患彌深何足與議禦邊之畧哉執
事以邊務為問慮至深遠也愚不敏敬悉
所聞以對夫夷狄之患自古難免小雅之
詩有云王命南仲城彼朔方是嘗飭邊備
矣又云方叔元老克壯其猶亦嘗振武威

===
羅一世之豪傑而鼓舞之假之以便宜而
不撓于中制則其機運矣人心思奮以必
勝爲期使敵人畏之而不敢犯則無形之
險在我矣否則其備彌周其道彌遠其慮
彌悉其患彌深何足與議禦邊之畧哉執
事以邊務爲問慮至深遠也愚不敏敬悉
所聞以對夫夷狄之患自古難免小雅之
詩有云王命南仲城彼朔方是嘗飭邊備
矣又云方叔元老克壯其猶亦嘗振武威
punctuated:
禁中頗牧者耶？

禦邊之畧有要焉，而泛者不與也；有機焉，而滯者不與也；有無形之險焉，而周防曲護者不與也。夫事幾之動，其變無常，議之者適中其肯綮之會，是之謂要。以天下非常之事，付之以非常之才，使之畢力以圖其成，是之謂機。委之專，任之久，俾上下之志固結而不可解，是之謂險。是故務安攘之大計，而不恬於旦夕之安，則其要得矣；羅一世之豪傑而鼓舞之，假之以便宜而不撓于中制，則其機運矣；人心思奮，以必勝為期，使敵人畏之而不敢犯，則無形之險在我矣。否則，其備彌周，其道彌遠；其慮彌悉，其患彌深。何足與議禦邊之畧哉！執事以邊務為問，慮至深遠也。愚不敏，敬悉所聞以對。夫夷狄之患，自古難免。《小雅》之詩有云：「王命南仲，城彼朔方。」是嘗飭邊備矣。又云：「方叔元老，克壯其猶。」亦嘗振武威
translation_en:
…a Lian Po or Li Mu within the palace?

The strategy for defending the frontiers has essentials that those who speak in generalities cannot grasp; it has opportunities that the inflexible cannot seize; and it has intangible defenses that those who guard every point and protect every corner cannot attain. When affairs begin to stir, their changes follow no constant course. To deliberate upon them and strike precisely at their crucial juncture is what is meant by grasping the essentials. To entrust the extraordinary affairs of the realm to men of extraordinary ability, and have them exert their utmost strength to bring those affairs to a successful conclusion, is what is meant by seizing opportunities. To give them undivided responsibility and retain them long in office, so that the resolve of superiors and subordinates becomes firmly united and cannot be sundered, is what is meant by establishing defenses. Thus, if one pursues the great plan of securing peace within and repelling enemies without, rather than resting content with momentary security, the essentials will be grasped. If one gathers and inspires the outstanding men of the age, grants them discretion to act as circumstances require, and does not hamper them through control from the court, opportunities will be put to use. If men are eager to exert themselves and set their sights on certain victory, causing the enemy to fear them and dare not invade, then intangible defenses will be ours. Otherwise, the more comprehensive the preparations, the further one strays from the proper course; the more exhaustive the deliberations, the deeper the troubles. How could such men be qualified to discuss the strategy for defending the frontiers?

You, honored examiners, have asked about frontier affairs: your concerns are most profound and far-reaching. Dull-witted though I am, I respectfully offer all that I have heard in reply. Trouble from the Yi and Di peoples has been difficult to avoid since antiquity. A poem in the Lesser Odes says: “The king commanded Nan Zhong to build fortifications there in Shuofang.” Thus frontier defenses were indeed put in order. Another says: “Fang Shu, the venerable elder, was mighty in his counsels.” Thus military might, too, was once displayed…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矣蓋由宣王内修以壯中國之勢外攘以
消夷狄之橫故朔方之城荆蠻之伐所不
能已也嚴尤曰周得中策漢得下策秦無
策劉貺曰周得上策秦得中策漢無策自
今觀之周之修内禦外貺謂上策則誠然
矣而秦之長城困役漢之約親損威其失
則一也何足論邪嗣是以還代有強弱逮
我
太祖肅清函夏汛掃腥膻
===
成祖定鼎幽燕親逐戎虜使華夷中外之勢截
然如天澤之異位此其
神謀睿筭高出千古有非前代所能彷彿其萬
一也然承平日久武備寢弛群孽匪茹數
擾内地邇年以来西寇雲中南犯太原北
侵上谷東襲遼陽中外騷然遠近震惕將
士疲於奔命齊民困於轉輸至於上煩
宵旰之憂者非一日矣頃者

punctuated:
矣。蓋由宣王内修以壯中國之勢，外攘以消夷狄之橫，故朔方之城、荆蠻之伐，所不能已也。嚴尤曰：「周得中策，漢得下策，秦無策。」劉貺曰：「周得上策，秦得中策，漢無策。」自今觀之，周之修内禦外，貺謂上策，則誠然矣。而秦之長城困役，漢之約親損威，其失則一也，何足論邪？
嗣是以還，代有強弱。逮我太祖肅清函夏，汛掃腥膻；成祖定鼎幽燕，親逐戎虜，使華夷中外之勢截然，如天澤之異位。此其神謀睿筭，高出千古，有非前代所能彷彿其萬一也。
然承平日久，武備寢弛，群孽匪茹，數擾内地。邇年以来，西寇雲中，南犯太原，北侵上谷，東襲遼陽，中外騷然，遠近震惕。將士疲於奔命，齊民困於轉輸，至於上煩宵旰之憂者，非一日矣。頃者，京師地震。
translation_en:
…as well. This was because King Xuan strengthened the Central States through internal reform and curbed the aggressiveness of the barbarians by repelling them abroad. Thus, fortifying Shuofang and campaigning against the Man of Jing were unavoidable. Yan You said: “Zhou adopted the middling policy; Han adopted the inferior policy; Qin had no policy.” Liu Kuang said: “Zhou adopted the best policy; Qin adopted the middling policy; Han had no policy.” Viewed from the present, Zhou’s internal reform and external defense were indeed, as Kuang said, the best policy. Yet Qin exhausted its people with labor on the Great Wall, while Han diminished its prestige through marriage alliances. Their failures were alike: what distinction is worth debating?
From that time onward, successive dynasties varied in strength. Then our Taizu pacified all the Chinese lands and swept away the rank and fetid barbarians. Chengzu established his capital in You and Yan and personally drove out the barbarian foes, making the division between Chinese and barbarians, inner realm and outer regions, as distinct as the separate positions of heaven and marsh. His inspired plans and sagacious calculations surpassed those of all antiquity; earlier dynasties could not approach even one ten-thousandth of his achievement.
Yet after prolonged peace, military preparedness gradually slackened. The bands of evildoers showed no restraint and repeatedly disturbed the interior. In recent years, they have raided Yunzhong in the west, attacked Taiyuan to the south, invaded Shanggu to the north, and struck Liaoyang to the east. The court and the provinces have been thrown into turmoil, and people near and far tremble in alarm. Officers and soldiers are exhausted from rushing to meet emergencies, and ordinary people are worn down by transporting supplies. That these troubles have burdened Your Majesty with anxiety, keeping you occupied before dawn and late into the night, is no recent development. Recently, an earthquake struck the capital.

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上開發言路詔陳政事得失一時獻計諸臣
無慮百數然而事緒轉多支吾不暇紛紜
可否迄無定裁議者謂守必資於地形是
矣今延袤千里版築蝟興則金湯之勢非
不屹然壯也謂戰必資於士馬是矣今聯
翩萬竈鐵騎雲屯則貔貅之衆非不裒然
集也顧邊警一作輒爾告急而安攘之效
猶茫然未覩此可不深求其故邪愚嘗反
覆古今之變窮探事理之極而有以得其
槩矣蓋天下之大事必因才而後成天下
之大機必因人而後運逸其才而不用逆
其機而緩圖是皆不足與議天下之務也
詩曰大邦維翰書曰以蕃王室人才之於
國家固將有以翰蕃之矣今有人宅於山
者知猛獸之爲害也則必外設窞穽内固
柴援以防之猶必擇機警有力之伇以伺
之苟防衛徒飭而伺守或疎則獸將乗間
而入矣方今之勢何以異此而議之者但

punctuated: 皇上開發言路，詔陳政事得失。一時獻計諸臣，無慮百數。然而事緒轉多，支吾不暇，紛紜可否，迄無定裁。議者謂守必資於地形，是矣。今延袤千里，版築蝟興，則金湯之勢非不屹然壯也。謂戰必資於士馬，是矣。今聯翩萬竈，鐵騎雲屯，則貔貅之衆非不裒然集也。顧邊警一作，輒爾告急，而安攘之效猶茫然未覩，此可不深求其故邪？愚嘗反覆古今之變，窮探事理之極，而有以得其槩矣。蓋天下之大事，必因才而後成；天下之大機，必因人而後運。逸其才而不用，逆其機而緩圖，是皆不足與議天下之務也。詩曰：「大邦維翰。」書曰：「以蕃王室。」人才之於國家，固將有以翰蕃之矣。今有人宅於山者，知猛獸之爲害也，則必外設窞穽，内固柴援以防之，猶必擇機警有力之伇以伺之。苟防衛徒飭，而伺守或疎，則獸將乗間而入矣。方今之勢，何以異此？而議之者但
translation_en:
…His Majesty opened the channels for expressing opinions and issued an edict calling for accounts of the successes and failings of government. At once, officials offering proposals numbered fully in the hundreds. Yet the matters to be handled only multiplied, leaving no time even to cope with them; amid conflicting opinions for and against, no definitive decision has yet been reached. Those discussing the matter say that defense must depend on the terrain. This is true. Today, over a thousand li, rammed-earth fortifications spring up like hedgehog spines: our defenses, as impregnable as metal walls and boiling moats, certainly stand imposing and strong. They say that battle must depend on soldiers and horses. This too is true. Today, ten thousand camp stoves stretch in succession, and armored cavalry muster like clouds: our tiger-like hosts have certainly assembled in great numbers. Yet whenever an alarm arises on the frontier, urgent appeals immediately follow, while any success in securing peace at home and repelling enemies abroad remains nowhere to be seen. Can we fail to investigate its cause deeply?

I have repeatedly considered the changes of past and present and probed the principles underlying affairs to their utmost extent, and have thereby grasped their general outline. Great undertakings in the realm can be accomplished only through talent; the great workings of the realm can be set in motion only through people. Those who leave talent idle and unused, and who act against the opportune moment and delay their plans, are unfit to deliberate on the affairs of the realm. The Book of Odes says, “The great states are supporting pillars.” The Book of Documents says, “To serve as a bulwark for the royal house.” Talented people must indeed serve the state as its pillars and bulwarks.

Suppose someone lives in the mountains. Knowing the harm that fierce beasts can do, he will certainly set pits and traps outside and strengthen his timber palisade within to ward them off. Still, he must also select alert and strong servants to keep watch for them. If defensive precautions are merely put in order, while the watch is at all lax, the beasts will seize an opening and enter. How does the present situation differ from this? Yet those discussing it merely…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
曰無兵也無險也無財用也無禦戎之策
也伏思
國家創業之初四方割據中原地狹兵財不
多尚能混一區宇殄滅強胡豈如今日承
百九十年
祖宗之業盡有天下之富疆復據上游之形勝
顧欲折衝則常患無兵欲屏蔽則常患無
險欲餽給則常患無財用欲威四夷則常
患無策此其故何邪蓋求之未得其術耳
===
求之未得其術者以用之未得其人也其
人茍得則萬務可辦矧唯禦虜之一事乎
故曰有要焉而泛者不與也且天生人才
自足以供一代之用昔雄畧如漢武帝誅
滅四夷立功萬里欲求將則有衛霍之材
以供其指示欲得賢士則有董汲之徒以
稱其意聰明如唐太宗誅突厥服遼東威
震夷狄欲求將則有李靖李勣之徒入其
駕馭欲得賢士則有房魏之徒在其任使

punctuated: 曰：「無兵也，無險也，無財用也，無禦戎之策也。」伏思國家創業之初，四方割據，中原地狹，兵財不多，尚能混一區宇，殄滅強胡。豈如今日，承百九十年祖宗之業，盡有天下之富疆，復據上游之形勝，顧欲折衝則常患無兵，欲屏蔽則常患無險，欲餽給則常患無財用，欲威四夷則常患無策，此其故何邪？蓋求之未得其術耳。求之未得其術者，以用之未得其人也。其人茍得，則萬務可辦，矧唯禦虜之一事乎？故曰：「有要焉，而泛者不與也。」且天生人才，自足以供一代之用。昔雄畧如漢武帝，誅滅四夷，立功萬里，欲求將則有衛霍之材以供其指示，欲得賢士則有董汲之徒以稱其意。聰明如唐太宗，誅突厥，服遼東，威震夷狄，欲求將則有李靖李勣之徒入其駕馭，欲得賢士則有房魏之徒在其任使。
translation_en:
…say: “We have no troops, no natural defenses, no financial resources, and no strategy for resisting the foreign enemy.” I humbly reflect that, when our dynasty was first founded, rival powers held separate territories in every direction. Its territory in the Central Plain was small, and its troops and resources were few; yet it could still unite the realm and destroy the powerful northern foes. How could those circumstances compare with today, when we inherit the achievements of our imperial ancestors over one hundred and ninety years, possess all the wealth and territory of the realm, and also command the strategic advantages of an upstream position? Yet whenever we wish to repel aggression, we constantly lament a lack of troops; whenever we wish to provide protection, a lack of natural defenses; whenever we wish to furnish supplies, a lack of financial resources; and whenever we wish to overawe the peoples of the four quarters, a lack of strategy. Why is this? It is simply that we have not found the proper method of seeking these things.

We have not found the proper method because we have not obtained the right people to employ. Once the right people are obtained, every affair can be managed—how much more so the single matter of resisting the enemy! Thus I say: “There is an essential point here, which those who deal only in generalities cannot grasp.” Moreover, Heaven produces enough talented people to meet the needs of each age. In former times, Emperor Wu of Han, with his heroic strategic ability, destroyed enemies in the four quarters and achieved victories ten thousand li away. When he sought generals, there were men of the talent of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing to carry out his commands; when he sought worthy men, there were men such as Dong Zhongshu and Ji An to meet his wishes. Emperor Taizong of Tang, with his intelligence and discernment, crushed the Tujue, subdued Liaodong, and made his might felt among foreign peoples. When he sought generals, there were men such as Li Jing and Li Ji to serve under his command; when he sought worthy men, there were men such as Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng to serve in his appointments.

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
孔子曰十室之邑必有忠信況今
聖明在上邁迹周宣漢武唐宗弗屑也而文武
列職又徧於天下其間豈無材智卓犖之
士以乘時附運顧患其不足於用邪柰何
今之覈撫臣者不察其能否但云孰可當
鉅鎮孰可調偏綏也簡將領者不問其優
劣但云某宜於邊方某宜於腹裏也嗚呼
此皆遷就之說也愚聞用人者惟取其優
於統御優於輯寧優於籌畧矣未聞有所
===
謂宜鉅鎮宜偏綏也惟取其一軍之將百
里之將千里之將矣未聞有所謂宜邊方
宜腹裏也苟其人可用則用之不可則易
之若賢愚雜混僥倖相容後時敗事徒耗
國而粍民咎將誰諉哉故曰有機會而滯
者不與也為今之計誠能革去舊弊奮然
精求有賢豪之士不須限以下位有智畧
之人不必索以微瑕有山林之傑不可薄
其疎賤使司督撫者抱良平之器膺將領

punctuated: 孔子曰：「十室之邑，必有忠信。」況今聖明在上，邁迹周宣、漢武、唐宗，弗屑也。而文武列職又徧於天下，其間豈無材智卓犖之士，以乘時附運，顧患其不足於用邪？柰何今之覈撫臣者，不察其能否，但云孰可當鉅鎮，孰可調偏綏也；簡將領者，不問其優劣，但云某宜於邊方，某宜於腹裏也。嗚呼！此皆遷就之說也。愚聞用人者，惟取其優於統御、優於輯寧、優於籌畧矣，未聞有所謂宜鉅鎮、宜偏綏也；惟取其一軍之將、百里之將、千里之將矣，未聞有所謂宜邊方、宜腹裏也。苟其人可用則用之，不可則易之。若賢愚雜混，僥倖相容，後時敗事，徒耗國而粍民，咎將誰諉哉？故曰：「有機會而滯者不與也。」為今之計，誠能革去舊弊，奮然精求，有賢豪之士，不須限以下位；有智畧之人，不必索以微瑕；有山林之傑，不可薄其疎賤。使司督撫者抱良平之器，膺將領
translation_en:
Confucius said, “Even in a settlement of ten households, there are sure to be people who are loyal and trustworthy.” How much more so now, with our sagacious sovereign above us, surpassing the achievements of King Xuan of Zhou, Emperor Wu of Han, and Emperor Taizong of Tang, and disdaining merely to match them. Civil and military posts extend throughout the realm. Could there be no men among their occupants of outstanding ability and intelligence, ready to seize the moment and serve the fortunes of the age? Why worry that there are too few to employ? Yet why do those who now assess grand coordinators fail to examine their competence, saying only who can take charge of a major garrison and who can be transferred to a lesser pacification command [?]? Those who select military commanders do not inquire into their strengths and weaknesses, saying only that one man is suited to the frontier and another to the interior. Alas! These are all arguments for expedient accommodation.

I have heard that those who employ men select them solely for excellence in command, in securing peace, and in strategic planning. I have never heard of such distinctions as suitability for a major garrison or for a lesser pacification command [?]. They select men according to their capacity to command an army, a territory of a hundred li, or a territory of a thousand li. I have never heard of such distinctions as suitability for the frontier or for the interior. If a man is fit to serve, employ him; if not, replace him. If worthy men and fools are indiscriminately mixed together and allowed to remain through mere good fortune, missing the proper moment and ruining affairs, doing nothing but exhausting the state and wearing down the people, upon whom will the blame be shifted? Thus I say, “There are opportunities, but those who remain inert have no part in them.”

For present purposes, if we can truly eliminate longstanding abuses and resolutely seek out talent with care, then men of worth and heroic capacity need not be confined to lowly positions; men of intelligence and strategic ability need not be scrutinized for trivial flaws; and outstanding men living in retirement among the mountains and forests must not be slighted for their remoteness from office and humble standing. Let those serving as supreme commanders and grand coordinators possess the capacity of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, and those appointed as military commanders …

者負韓白之才分閫授兵必李牧魏尚其
人焉據險阻隘必張仁愿王忠嗣其人焉
有趙充國班超之望者即以拊綏征討之
事屬之有唐休璟張守珪之畧者即以簡
練招懷之任畀之然後假之以事權遲之
以歲月責之以措置天下之務乘閒暇之
時治其戰攻守禦之具兼聽博採以周知
敵人之虛實在上者又握其樞而運之歆
以不次之遷懸以不貲之賞優之以禮而

裨偏裨率士卒文武兼濟上下相維蓋

translation_en: …should possess the talents of Han Xin and Bai Qi. Those assigned independent commands and entrusted with troops must be men like Li Mu and Wei Shang; those holding strategic terrain and blocking narrow passes must be men like Zhang Renyuan and Wang Zhongsi. Anyone with the standing of Zhao Chongguo or Ban Chao should be entrusted with pacification and punitive campaigns; anyone with the strategic ability of Tang Xiujing or Zhang Shougui should be charged with selecting and training troops and winning people over. Then grant them authority to act, allow them months and years, and hold them responsible for managing the affairs of the realm. They should use periods of respite to prepare the equipment for battle, attack, and defense, listening widely and gathering information broadly so as to know thoroughly the enemy’s strengths and weaknesses. Those above them should retain control of the directing mechanism and set it in motion, enticing them with promotion outside the normal sequence, offering rewards of immense value, treating them generously with due ceremony, and extending sincere trust to them. When trouble arises, the Supreme Commander should issue instructions to the Regional Commanders and Grand Coordinators, who should hold subordinate commanders responsible; these in turn should lead the officers and soldiers. Civil and military officials should complement one another, and superiors and subordinates should support one another. When the state employs talented men with exceptional courtesy, they in turn will repay the state with exceptional achievements. Who would not cherish his own reputation and exert himself, hoping to establish extraordinary accomplishments in his own time and leave an illustrious name to posterity? Thus, they may refrain from defending, but whenever they defend, their defenses will be secure; they may refrain from fighting, but whenever they fight, they will prevail. If this approach is used to resist the barbarians, their designs to watch for opportunities can be dispelled without further action, and their aggressive spirit can be imperceptibly broken. Is this method not exceedingly simple? To set it aside without pursuing it, and instead anxiously seek only to strengthen defensive positions and increase garrison quotas, claiming that this will suffice to secure peace within and repel threats from without—even the most foolish know…

皇上膺天眷命，嗣承祖宗弘大靈長之業，丕闡人文，以化成天下。謂科目盛典，寔惟敷求俊乂，以共天職，尤惓惓焉。嘉靖己酉秋八月，復當鄉試之期，順天府臣循例以聞。上特詔臣樸偕侍講臣大和往司文柄。臣樸竊念，曩歲嘗以職事分校禮闈，又嘗典試武會，至是凡三命焉。任愈重，則責愈難塞，敢不愼諸？暨
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

His Majesty received Heaven’s gracious mandate and succeeded to the vast and enduring enterprise of his imperial ancestors. He has greatly promoted literary culture, thereby transforming and perfecting the realm. He regards the grand institution of the examinations as a means of seeking out outstanding talent far and wide to share in the duties entrusted by Heaven, and devotes particular care to it. In the eighth month of autumn in the jiyou year of Jiajing [1549], the time for the Provincial Examination came round again. The officials of Shuntian Prefecture reported this to the throne in accordance with precedent. His Majesty specially commanded your servant Pu, together with your servant Dahe, Expositor, to go and take charge of the literary selection.

Your servant Pu reflected that in earlier years, as part of my official duties, I had served as an Associate Examiner in the Metropolitan Examination, and had also presided over the military Metropolitan Examination. With this appointment, I have now received three such commands. The weightier the charge, the harder it is to discharge the responsibility fully. How could I dare be anything but circumspect? When…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
陛辭入院則相率諸同事者誓公
誓精悉竭心力以從事既取士
如式爰列其姓氏及文之粹者
爲錄以
獻且以傳示海內臣謹序其後曰
宋蘇軾有言君子之得其君也
既度其君又度其身君能之而
===
我不能不敢進也我能之而君
不能不可爲也夫自古有志之
士不爲少矣孰不欲其道之行
哉然恒以遭遇爲難故必得大
有爲之君然後道之在我者始
可乘時而售之用惟爾諸士舉
于鄉升于有司行且嗣服有位

punctuated:
陛辭入院，則相率諸同事者誓公誓精，悉竭心力以從事。既取士如式，爰列其姓氏及文之粹者爲錄，以獻，且以傳示海內。臣謹序其後曰：
宋蘇軾有言：「君子之得其君也，既度其君，又度其身。君能之而我不能，不敢進也；我能之而君不能，不可爲也。」夫自古有志之士不爲少矣，孰不欲其道之行哉？然恒以遭遇爲難，故必得大有爲之君，然後道之在我者始可乘時而售之用。惟爾諸士，舉于鄉，升于有司，行且嗣服有位，
translation_en:
…upon taking leave of Your Majesty and entering the examination compound, we led all our colleagues in pledging impartiality and care, devoting our whole minds and strength to the task. Having selected candidates according to the prescribed procedures, we compiled their names and the finest of their writings into a record, to present to Your Majesty and also to circulate throughout the realm. Your servant respectfully appends these prefatory remarks:
Su Shi of the Song dynasty said: “When a gentleman finds his ruler, he assesses both his ruler and himself. If the ruler is capable but I am not, I dare not advance into service; if I am capable but the ruler is not, nothing can be accomplished.” Since antiquity, men of aspiration have been numerous. Who among them has not wished to see his Way put into practice? Yet they have always found it difficult to encounter a favorable opportunity. Only upon finding a ruler capable of great achievement can they seize the moment and bring the Way they possess into practical use. You scholars, recommended through the Provincial Examination and advanced to the responsible authorities, will soon take up official positions in your turn…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
亦既度其能而進之矣際昇平
之世應
聖作之期又得
大有爲之君以事之士而値此豈非
千載一時之會哉夫人幼而學
於家也其志不同故其得有淺
深而其成功有巨細雖其終身
===
之所爲不可逆知而其大節必
見於始進之日何者其中素定
也孔子曰事君先資其言拜自
獻其身以成其信今茲所試固
爾諸士自獻先資之言也果能
一一以成其信乎夫堯舜其君
而使無一夫之不獲夫人類能

punctuated: 亦既度其能而進之矣。際昇平之世，應聖作之期，又得大有爲之君以事之，士而値此，豈非千載一時之會哉！夫人幼而學於家也，其志不同，故其得有淺深，而其成功有巨細。雖其終身之所爲不可逆知，而其大節必見於始進之日。何者？其中素定也。孔子曰：「事君，先資其言，拜自獻其身以成其信。」今茲所試，固爾諸士自獻先資之言也，果能一一以成其信乎？夫堯舜其君，而使無一夫之不獲，夫人類能
translation_en: …your abilities have already been assessed, and you have been advanced accordingly. You encounter an age of peace and prosperity, at a time when a sage sovereign arises, and moreover have a ruler capable of great achievements to serve. For scholars to meet with such circumstances—is this not an opportunity that comes but once in a thousand years? People study at home from childhood, but their aspirations differ; hence their attainments vary in depth, and their accomplishments in magnitude. Although what they will do throughout their lives cannot be known beforehand, their fundamental principles will surely reveal themselves when they first enter service. Why is this? Because their inward resolve has long been settled. Confucius said: “In serving a ruler, first offer your words as a pledge; bow and present yourself [?], thereby making good your word.” What you scholars have written in this examination is precisely such a pledge, offered as you present yourselves for service. Can you truly make good each and every word? As for making your ruler a Yao or a Shun and ensuring that not a single person fails to receive his due, everyone can…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
言之而君子獨許夫伊尹者為
能充其志以信其言也今觀諸
士之文頌必唐虞稽必堯舜凡
一切功利之說悉置不齒亦何
異伊尹之畝畝自許者乎
聖明在上道本心傳統宗會極亦何
異堯舜之再出者乎惟兹延攬
===
無方禮羅駢設進一世之豪傑
而登崇之亦何異有商之聘于
莘野者乎夫諸士之文美矣其
志與所得亦畧見矣不知異日
功業所到亦能充其志以信其
言如古之伊尹否也夫士之進
而不度其能是謂自欺度君之

而登崇之亦何異有商之聘于

志與所得亦畧見矣不知異日
功業所到亦能充其志以信其
言如古之伊尹否也夫士之進
而不度其能是謂自欺度君之
punctuated: 言之，而君子獨許夫伊尹者，為能充其志以信其言也。今觀諸士之文，頌必唐虞，稽必堯舜，凡一切功利之說悉置不齒，亦何異伊尹之畝畝自許者乎？聖明在上，道本心傳，統宗會極，亦何異堯舜之再出者乎？惟兹延攬無方，禮羅駢設，進一世之豪傑而登崇之，亦何異有商之聘于莘野者乎？夫諸士之文美矣，其志與所得亦畧見矣。不知異日功業所到，亦能充其志以信其言，如古之伊尹否也？夫士之進而不度其能，是謂自欺；度君之
translation_en:
…say this, yet gentlemen accord recognition to Yi Yin alone because he could fulfill his aspirations and thus make good his words. Looking now at your essays, gentlemen, whenever you offer praise, it is of Tang and Yu; whenever you invoke precedents, they are Yao and Shun. You dismiss all doctrines of material achievement and advantage as unworthy of mention. How does this differ from the aspirations Yi Yin professed while among the fields [?]?

Our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above; the Way is rooted in the transmission of the mind, and the succession takes as its guiding principle convergence upon the supreme standard. How does this differ from Yao and Shun appearing once again? Now worthy men are being recruited without restriction, and the ceremonial means of drawing them in are deployed in abundance. The outstanding men of an entire age are advanced and raised to honored positions. How does this differ from the Shang ruler’s invitation to Yi Yin in the fields of Shen?

Your essays, gentlemen, are excellent, and your aspirations and attainments are already somewhat apparent. Yet I wonder whether, in the achievements you reach in days to come, you will also be able to fulfill your aspirations and make good your words, like Yi Yin of antiquity. When a scholar advances into office without assessing his own ability, this is called deceiving himself; to assess one’s ruler’s…

title: 嘉靖二十八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
能而不以堯舜之道事之是謂
欺君是二者皆弊也文之美奚
足尚哉易有之聖人養賢以及
萬民
國家之所以望於科目者則厚矣
爾諸士産於
畿甸或来自四國服膺
===
聖化既深且乆是舉也豈無為德為
民若伊尹者出以應其求哉於
戲士而不遇無可言者用而弗
績咎将奚歸致用之大端姑驗
於一第而其逺者大者邈乎不
在是也傳曰志伊尹之所志士
而不以伊尹自期非士矣盍相

punctuated:
能，而不以堯舜之道事之，是謂欺君。是二者皆弊也，文之美奚足尚哉？易有之：「聖人養賢以及萬民。」國家之所以望於科目者則厚矣。
爾諸士産於畿甸，或来自四國，服膺聖化既深且乆。是舉也，豈無為德為民若伊尹者出，以應其求哉？於戲！士而不遇，無可言者；用而弗績，咎将奚歸？致用之大端，姑驗於一第，而其逺者大者，邈乎不在是也。傳曰：「志伊尹之所志。」士而不以伊尹自期，非士矣。盍相
translation_en:
…capacity, yet does not serve him according to the Way of Yao and Shun: this is called deceiving the ruler. Both these are failings. What, then, is there to esteem in the beauty of literary composition alone? The Book of Changes says: “The sage nourishes the worthy, and thereby extends nourishment to the myriad people.” The state’s expectations of the examination system are thus weighty indeed.
You scholars were born in the metropolitan region, or came from the four quarters, and have long and deeply embraced the sage ruler’s transforming influence. In this examination, surely some who work for virtue and for the people, like Yi Yin, will come forward to answer the state’s search? Alas! If a scholar has no opportunity to serve, there is nothing to say; but if he is employed and achieves nothing, where will the blame fall? The essential capacity to put learning into practice is provisionally tested by success in an examination; yet its far-reaching and greater manifestations lie far beyond this. The commentary says: “Aspire to what Yi Yin aspired to.” A scholar who does not take Yi Yin as the standard for his own aspirations is no scholar. Why not together …
